security_spec.violation_condition: On a Ziccid platform, the kernel relies on FENCE.I for I-D coherence after text patching (bpftrace, kprobes, ftrace, alternatives, module loading). If FENCE.I is executed on a hart other than the one that performed the store, and Ziccid's 'eventuality' property is relied upon without proper synchronization (FENCE W,O + IPI or FENCE W,W + flag + remote FENCE.I), the remote hart may indefinitely execute stale instructions because Ziccid explicitly scopes instruction-fetch ordering to the local hart — instruction fetches only appear in program order *per hart*, and cross-hart visibility of stores to instruction fetches requires explicit synchronization in addition to FENCE.I. The kernel's existing stop_machine()/on_each_cpu() FENCE.I broadcast pattern in patch_text() and flush_icache_mm() already handles this correctly. The vulnerable pattern would be code that performs a local FENCE.I after a store on one hart and expects another hart to eventually see the store via Ziccid's eventuality guarantee, without the required FENCE W,O+IPI or FENCE W,W+flag synchronization that the spec explicitly requires for cross-hart I-fetch visibility.
security_spec.summary: Ziccid's I-fetch ordering is per-hart; cross-hart I-D coherence still requires FENCE W,O + IPI-triggered remote FENCE.I — kernel code patches that assume Ziccid eliminates the need for cross-hart fencing would cause remote harts to execute stale instructions

findings.finding: Bare 'fence.i' primitive, correctly documented as local-only. As the fundamental building block, it is never relied upon for cross-hart I-D coherence without proper synchronization.

spec_citations.excerpt: A FENCE.I instruction ensures that a subsequent instruction fetch on a RISC-V hart will see any previous data stores already visible to the same RISC-V hart. FENCE.I does _not_ ensure that other RISC-V harts' instruction fetches will observe the local hart's stores in a multiprocessor system. To make a store to instruction memory visible to all RISC-V harts, the writing hart also has to execute a data FENCE before requesting that all remote RISC-V harts execute a FENCE.I.

findings.finding: Correctly implements the spec-mandated cross-hart pattern: local FENCE.I on writer, then RISCV_FENCE(w,o) to order prior stores before the IPI/MMIO write that triggers remote FENCE.I via sbi_remote_fence_i() or on_each_cpu().

findings.finding: Correct cross-hart I-D coherence for MM context: sets stale mask for all harts, does local FENCE.I on caller, then sends remote FENCE.I (via SBI or on_each_cpu_mask) to harts running this MM. The smp_mb() in the deferred path pairs with smp_mb() in flush_icache_deferred() for harts not currently running the MM.

findings.finding: Context-switch deferred flush: smp_mb() pairs with writer's barrier in flush_icache_mm() to ensure remote stores are visible before the local FENCE.I on the newly-scheduled hart. This implements the FENCE W,W + flag + local FENCE.I pattern correctly.

findings.finding: stop_machine() rendezvous with correct synchronization: writer CPU does atomic_inc_return_release (FENCE W,W release), other CPUs spin-wait then do local_flush_icache_all(). The RELEASE + local FENCE.I pattern on each remote hart ensures the writer's stores are visible before FENCE.I executes.

findings.finding: Does patch_insn_write (local FENCE.I on writer via __patch_insn_write) then flush_icache_range → flush_icache_all() which performs FENCE W,O + remote FENCE.I. The inner local flush is an optimization; the outer flush_icache_all provides the required cross-hart synchronization.

findings.finding: Secondary CPU boot-time precautionary flush. The CPU was offline and missed prior FENCE.I broadcasts, so flushing now before enabling interrupts is correct. No cross-hart concern — this is self-flush after onlining.
Kexec path: all other CPUs are stopped via CPU hotplug before reaching this point, so a local FENCE.I is sufficient to make the relocation code visible to the sole remaining hart.
findings.snippet:
/* Make sure the relocation code is visible to the hart */
local_flush_icache_all();

findings.finding: EARLY_BOOT stage: only the boot CPU is running (SMP not yet initialized), so memcpy + local FENCE.I is sufficient. Non-early stage uses patch_text_nosync which calls flush_icache_all() with full cross-hart synchronization.

User-space icache flush on task migration. Only flushes when switch_to_should_flush_icache() is true (thread migrated + force_icache_flush set). This handles the case where userspace uses fence.i and then migrates — the new hart gets a flush. On Ziccid, migration still requires this flush since the new hart hasn't seen the prior stores.

spec_citations.excerpt: The FENCE.I only synchronizes the local hart, and the OS can reschedule the user hart to a different physical hart after the FENCE.I. This would require the OS to execute an additional FENCE.I as part of every context migration.

findings.finding: Membarrier sync_core path: called from ipi_sync_core() which runs on remote CPUs via IPI. The IPI + smp_mb() in the membarrier path provides cross-hart ordering, then the local fence.i on each remote hart provides instruction-fetch coherence. This is the FENCE W,W + IPI + fence.i pattern.

findings.finding: Virtualizes guest fence.i with local_flush_icache_all(). Correct: the guest's fence.i only orders stores visible to the same vCPU, and the host's local FENCE.I achieves this. Cross-vCPU I-D coherence in the guest is the guest's responsibility (it would need its own cross-hart sync).

findings.finding: VDSO flush: on SMP uses syscall (sys_riscv_flush_icache → flush_icache_mm with full cross-hart sync); on UP uses bare fence.i which is correct since there are no other harts.
Early boot (M-mode) fence.i: only the boot hart is running at this point. No cross-hart concern.
Kexec relocation: the relocation code was just copied, and this runs on the sole surviving hart after all other CPUs are stopped. Local fence.i is sufficient.
findings.snippet:
/*
 * Make sure the relocated code is visible
 * and jump to the new kernel
 */
fence.i

findings.finding: Uses patch_text_nosync → patch_insn_write + flush_icache_all(). The outer flush_icache_all performs FENCE W,O + remote FENCE.I, satisfying the cross-hart synchronization requirement.
Uses patch_text_nosync which internally does local flush in __patch_insn_write + cross-hart flush_icache_all(). Correct.
Uses patch_text_nosync which calls patch_insn_write (local I$ flush on writer) then flush_icache_range → flush_icache_all() with FENCE W,O + remote FENCE.I. Cross-hart synchronization is satisfied.

BPF JIT code patching uses patch_text_nosync/patch_text_set_nosync under text_mutex, which internally does local flush + flush_icache_all() with full FENCE W,O + remote FENCE.I. Correct cross-hart synchronization.
